title: How many parallel lines appear after each fold?
description: A square sheet with two flat edges is folded in half again and again. The board counts the gaps and the parallel lines after one, two, three and four folds and reads the pattern. Keeko doubts that each fold adds only one line.
teaching_notes: One idea: each fold in half puts a new crease in every gap, so the gaps double and the parallel lines are always one more than the gaps. Watch for students who think each fold adds one line.

source: A square sheet has two flat edges. Fold it horizontally in half again and again. Count the parallel lines, including the two edges, after one, two, three and four folds. What is the pattern?
video_script.why: The child counts parallel lines on a folded sheet and sees how the count grows with each fold.
video_script.substitution: The book's own paper folding activity: a square sheet is folded horizontally in half, then once more, then again, and the parallel lines are counted after each fold.
video_script.anchor: A square sheet with two flat edges, with horizontal creases added by each fold in half.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks every fold adds only one crease, so the counts go up by one.
video_script.payoff_line: The counts are three, five, nine and seventeen, and the gaps double with every fold.

final_answer.value: 3, 5, 9 and 17 parallel lines; the gaps double and the lines are one more than the gaps
final_answer.spoken: three, five, nine and seventeen parallel lines; the gaps double and the lines are one more than the gaps

hold_back: 3, 5, 9 and 17 parallel lines; the gaps double and the lines are one more than the gaps
maths_rules: opposite edges of the sheet are parallel
after 1 fold: 2 gaps, so 2 + 1 = 3 parallel lines
after 2 folds: 4 gaps, so 4 + 1 = 5 parallel lines
after 3 folds: 8 gaps, so 8 + 1 = 9 parallel lines
after 4 folds: 16 gaps, so 16 + 1 = 17 parallel lines
every fold doubles the gaps: 2, 4, 8, 16; the lines are 1 more than the gaps: 3, 5, 9, 17
the slip: the counts 3, 4, 5, 6 add one line per fold, but each fold makes a new crease in every gap
video_script.design: One square sheet stays on the stage. Each fold adds creases in every gap, and the working band writes the gaps and the lines after each fold.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to count the parallel lines after each fold, and find the pattern.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 1 fold gives 2 gaps, so 2 + 1 = 3 lines; 2 folds give 4 gaps, so 4 + 1 = 5 lines

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, count after one fold and after two folds.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One fold makes two gaps, so there are two plus one parallel lines.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That is three lines, counting the two edges.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Two folds make four gaps, so there are four plus one lines, which is five.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 3 folds give 8 gaps, so 8 + 1 = 9 lines; 4 folds give 16 gaps, so 16 + 1 = 17 lines

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, count after three folds and after four folds.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Three folds make eight gaps, so there are eight plus one lines, which is nine.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Four folds make sixteen gaps, so there are sixteen plus one lines, which is seventeen.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, look at the pattern in the gaps and the lines.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks each fold adds one line, so the counts are three, four, five and six.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But a fold goes through every gap and puts a new crease in each one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The creases double with every fold, and they do not grow by one.
